clue.text: Might he make a mug out of Ronnie O'Sullivan?

definitions.text: Might he make a mug out of Ronnie O'Sullivan?

parts.words: Might he make a mug out of Ronnie O'Sullivan?
parts.note: a maker of mugs works clay at a wheel, while Ronnie O'Sullivan is a famous snooker player who sinks balls into pockets

explanation.surface: Someone wonders who could make the great snooker champion look a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a mug out of' reads as 'humiliate', but the mug is pottery. Ronnie O'Sullivan is a celebrated English snooker player, and a snooker player who sinks balls is also called by the same word as a ceramic craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a craftsman shaping clay pots and a snooker player who pockets balls.

clue.text: Turn up combative to begin with during fight in boozy night out

indicators.note: turning a word round reads its letters in the other order
puts that letter within the word for a fight

parts.note: a brawl is a rough fight

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone turns up spoiling for a scrap on a drunken evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reads as 'arrive', but 'Turn' is the reversal signal on 'up'; 'to begin with' takes the first letter of 'combative' and 'during' sets it inside the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour of several drinking houses in one evening, a drink in each, is a binge outing.

clue.text: Turkey, another creature with small feet

parts.note: TR is Turkey's international vehicle registration code
an otter is a creature, another besides the turkey
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A turkey and some other animal are both said to have tiny feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the bird, so 'another creature' seems apt, but it is the country, TR.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs' feet, cooked as food, are called by this name, and humorously so are human feet.

clue.text: Tree, more mature one

definitions.meaning: a small tree with white flowers and dark berries
the older of two people, or a senior person in a community

explanation.surface: A tree described as being older than another.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the berry-bearing shrub and someone senior in age.

clue.text: Person I suspect has right to be inside?

definitions.text: Person I suspect has right to be inside?

indicators.note: says the letter for right goes within the jumbled letters
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters of the words before it are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A police officer reasons that the suspect deserves to be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a verb, but it signals an anagram of PERSON I; 'to be inside' then puts R inside it. Read as a whole, the clue also describes a jailed person, someone who is 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'inside' is slang for serving time in jail, which is what a convict or detainee does.

clue.text: Quickly declare that dance is cancelled

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish folk dance
an event that is cancelled is off

explanation.surface: An announcer rushes to tell everyone the dance won't go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite a list rapidly and fluently is to rattle it off.

clue.text: High court has dinner cooked

indicators.note: food that has been cooked has been prepared and changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior judge has an evening meal prepared for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High court' suggests a British court, but it is the supreme council of ancient Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: The supreme council and tribunal of the Jews in ancient Jerusalem was their highest judicial body.

clue.text: Cocaine is one, for example

parts.note: cocaine is a local anaesthetic that deadens feeling, and 'one' is an example of a numeral

explanation.surface: A remark that cocaine is an example of some category.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'something that makes numb', the word fits cocaine, an anaesthetic; read normally, 'one' is an example of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that deadens sensation is one that numbs, while 'one' is a numeral.

clue.text: Hotplate's no good? That's a mystery

indicators.note: the hotplate is without the letter for good

parts.note: a griddle is a flat cooking plate; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A cook puzzles over why the hotplate has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotplate's no good' reads as 'the hob is broken', but it means GRIDDLE with no G.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling question or enigma that is hard to work out is a conundrum.

clue.text: VIP pantomime dame may have one

definitions.meaning: a very important person, a big shot
a large, outlandish hairpiece worn by the comic dame

explanation.surface: A celebrity and a pantomime dame are said to share something.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime dame is the comic female role in a British Christmas pantomime, traditionally played by a man in garish clothes and a huge wig.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means an important person and, read literally, a large hairpiece.

clue.text: Criticism of minor routes over accidents, essentially

parts.note: B roads are the lesser numbered roads in Britain, below A roads

indicators.note: taken as 'at its very core', keeping only the central three letters of the word accidents and discarding the rest

explanation.surface: Someone complains that small country lanes are where crashes happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' places the minor roads before the core letters IDE, taken from inside 'accidents'. In Britain a B road is a secondary road, lower in rank than an A road.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce verbal attack is named after the simultaneous firing of all guns on one side of a warship.

clue.text: Hill — famous one on reflection for rambler

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the other way round, so the name is read from its end

parts.note: Damon Hill is a famous Formula One world champion racing driver

explanation.surface: A walker thinks back on a well-known hill while rambling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill' and 'rambler' suggest hillwalking, but the Hill is Damon Hill, the 1996 Formula One champion; 'on reflection' turns his first name around.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home roams from place to place, much as a rambler roves.

clue.text: It turns but remains unchanged

definitions.note: a part that spins on an axle, such as helicopter blades, is something that turns

indicators.note: the word stays the same when its letters are taken in the other direction, which fits a thing that turns

parts.note: a part that spins on an axle, such as helicopter blades, is something that turns

explanation.surface: Something rotates yet somehow stays exactly as it was.
explanation.walkthrough: The word reads the same both ways, so turning it round leaves it unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter's blades or the spinning part of a motor is the component that revolves.

clue.text: Bread not cut before supper, say

parts.note: something not cut is entire or complete
supper is one example of an eating occasion

explanation.surface: An uncut loaf is served ahead of the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of brown loaf baked from flour that keeps the entire grain.

clue.text: Grotesque growth a feature of this beast

definitions.text: Grotesque growth a feature of this beast

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted and misshapen, so the following letters are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A nature guide notes an ugly lump typical of some animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grotesque growth' reads as a description of the beast's facial lumps, but 'Grotesque' signals an anagram of GROWTH A; the whole clue also describes the animal, whose name begins with a word for a skin lump.
explanation.definitionFit: The African wild pig is known for knobbly lumps on its face, so an ugly growth is indeed its feature.

clue.text: Black pudding is usually this hybrid

definitions.meaning: black pudding is a British sausage made of pig's blood mixed with fat and oatmeal, so roughly half of it is blood
a person or animal of mixed parentage

explanation.surface: A claim that black pudding is a mixed creation.
explanation.walkthrough: Black pudding is a British sausage made from blood with oatmeal and fat, so read literally its make-up is half of one ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with one parent of a given lineage is of mixed descent, as in Harry Potter's term.

clue.text: Light discharge

definitions.meaning: to light something is to set it burning or ignite it
to discharge someone is to sack them; to discharge a gun is to shoot it

explanation.surface: A short note about a lamp and something released.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to ignite and to dismiss from a job, or to shoot a weapon.

clue.text: Freezing Scots man requiring kettle?

parts.note: cauld is the Scots word for cold
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A chilly Scotsman needs something to boil water in.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'kettle' as a loose example: a big cooking pot rather than a kettle.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal cooking pot, like a witch's, is a vessel for boiling, broadly a kettle.

clue.text: Maintain quiet modesty's awfully perverse

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
reserve is restraint and modesty of manner

explanation.surface: Someone insists that keeping quiet and modest is a terribly twisted idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully perverse' is a second wordplay: an anagram of PERVERSE gives the same letters, so the clue builds the answer twice; the grammar records only P + RESERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something intact or in good condition is to keep it going unchanged.

clue.text: League of Nations held back by protocol breach

indicators.note: back says the contained letters are read in the reverse direction
held says the letters are contained within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diplomatic incident has the international body hampered by a breach of etiquette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'League of Nations' points to the historical body, but here it means any alliance of countries. 'Held' signals the letters held in 'protocol breach'; 'back' reads them in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of countries joined in an alliance with common interests is a political grouping of this kind.

clue.text: Taps yellow light in meeting room

parts.note: taps on a basin are marked C and H, for cold and hot
the amber light on traffic signals is the yellow one

explanation.surface: A tapping noise and a yellow light come from a meeting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taps' looks like a verb or tapping sound, but it means the cold and hot taps, C and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall where a council or legislature assembles is called a council's debating room.

clue.text: Fantastic beast's beginning to confirm nature's in trouble

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
something in trouble is in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: read as 'nature is', the 's being a link

explanation.surface: An environmental warning confirms that the natural world is in peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to' takes C from 'confirm'; 'in trouble' scrambles NATURE into ENTAUR. The 's after 'beast' stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythical creature of Greek legend, half man and half horse, is a fabulous monster.

clue.text: Angel fish enthrals cockney woman

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the fish holds the woman inside it

parts.note: the chub is a freshwater fish
a cockney drops the h, so 'her' is said as 'er

explanation.surface: An angelfish captivates a woman from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney is a working-class Londoner; cockneys drop initial H, so HER becomes ER. 'Angel fish' looks like one thing, but 'Angel' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A winged child in art, or a heavenly being of the second order, is a celestial spirit.

clue.text: Stand by — a repeated phrase is coming up — musical tip

indicators.note: in a down clue, something coming up reads from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a riff is a short repeated musical phrase

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A conductor tells musicians to be ready, a recurring refrain approaching, with a musical tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' reverses RIFF to FFIR in this down clue; 'tip' takes M from 'musical'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand by a statement is to uphold or assert it firmly.

clue.text: Cup for a small mouth?

parts.note: gob is slang for mouth and the suffix -let makes things smaller, so a little gob suggests a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which cup suits a child's small mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: GOB is British slang for mouth, and -LET is a diminutive ending, as in piglet.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking cup with a stem and foot, often of metal or glass, is a stemmed vessel.

clue.text: Pay for holiday, you say? That'll slow you down

indicators.note: says the phrase is spoken, giving the sound of a car part

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay, and a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether to cover the cost of a trip, then is warned it will be costly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' means pay for (as in foot the bill) and 'break' means holiday; spoken, the two words sound like the pedal.
explanation.definitionFit: The pedal-operated stopping mechanism in a car reduces the vehicle's speed.

clue.text: Eyes — not misty, peeled

indicators.note: peeling strips the outer skin, so the outermost letters come off

parts.note: a day that is not misty is clear of fog

explanation.surface: A spotter keeps eyes wide open on a clear day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyes' and 'peeled' suggest keeping one's eyes peeled, but 'Eyes' is a verb and 'peeled' removes the outer letters of FOGLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye someone, especially lecherously, is to stare at them in a leering way.

clue.text: Organisation poured beer regularly

indicators.note: takes letters at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: A company has beer poured at frequent intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of 'poured beer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious society of monks or knights, such as the Jesuits, is a formal body or fraternity.

clue.text: Primitive home, one with good facilities

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
facilities is a polite word for a lavatory, which the British call a loo

explanation.surface: An estate agent advertises a basic dwelling that boasts decent amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facilities' looks like amenities generally, but it is the euphemism for a toilet, LOO in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome built of snow blocks is a simple traditional dwelling.

clue.text: One makes mistakes more miserable when goofy nerd's involved

indicators.note: something involved is wrapped up within, so the jumbled letters go inside

parts.note: bluer means more sad or down

indicators.note: goofy means silly and clumsy, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: read as 'nerd is', the 's being a link

explanation.surface: Someone gets gloomier at work whenever a clumsy geek joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More miserable' is BLUER because 'blue' means sad; 'when' and the 's (read as 'is') are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungler who keeps making clumsy errors is a person prone to gaffes.

clue.text: Animal killers held in esteem, a tad, or scorn

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the phrase that follows, spanning several of its words

explanation.surface: Bullfighters are regarded with mixed respect and contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held in esteem' reads as a stock phrase, but 'held in' is the signal and 'esteem' starts the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullfighters deliver the final sword thrust that kills the bull in the ring.

clue.text: Claw right back almost to the beginning, revealing a pop star

indicators.note: moves the letter back towards the start of the word, stopping just short of it

parts.note: a crab's claw is a pincer

explanation.surface: An instruction to draw a claw back reveals a famous singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back almost to the beginning' moves R in PINCER from the end to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-named American singer from Minneapolis, famous for Purple Rain, was a pop icon.
